task_summary: Resolved broken user avatar photos after upload on /profile by identifying and fixing MinIO AWS SigV4 Host header HMAC signature mismatch (403 Forbidden). Implemented public direct streaming endpoint GET /api/users/:userId/avatar with HTTP cache headers (ETag, 304 Not Modified, Cache-Control), added Mongoose virtual avatarUrl with timestamp cache-busting, updated ProfilePage and Header to reset broken state and immediately refresh global user state, and verified end-to-end via Playwright live browser audit with naturalWidth=50px image rendering.
lessons_learned: Lesson: MinIO and AWS S3 presigned URLs include SignedHeaders=host in the AWS SigV4 HMAC calculation. In containerized Docker setups where internal service DNS (e.g. http://minio:9000) differs from browser-facing hosts (http://localhost:9000), naively string-replacing the host in presigned URLs invalidates the cryptographic signature, causing 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch errors.

Lesson learned: Global Express authentication middleware (e.g. app.use('/api', authenticate)) blocks standard browser tags from loading subresource endpoints because browsers do not attach Authorization Bearer headers to GET requests. Public asset streaming routes like GET /api/users/:userId/avatar must be mounted before the global authenticate middleware.

Prevention: When serving mutable user uploads (like avatars) stored under static object keys (avatars/:userId/profile), attach a query parameter cache-buster based on updatedAt (e.g. ?t=${updatedAt}) and serve with ETag and 304 Not Modified headers so browsers refresh immediately upon upload without incurring unnecessary re-downloads.
